title: Two-tape machine code format
statement: There is a code format for deterministic machines with two work tapes and binary tape symbols. A code records its number of states, a designated initial state, and a transition table; its serialization pairs the binary expansion of the state-count parameter with the unary initial-state index followed by the serialized table. The format has a table reader and an erased table skipper, a guard constant of $351$ bits per state, and the halting fallback machine described above; assembling a state count, initial state, and table recovers every code, and the reader and skipper satisfy the stated consistency and length properties.
hypotheses_covered: Codes represent two-work-tape machines over Boolean symbols with states indexed by Fin (n + 1).
The state-count parameter of an assembled code is n.
Serialization uses the paired binary state-count encoding, unary initial-state encoding, and table bits.
Every code is obtained by assembling some state count, initial state, and table.
Reading serialized table bits followed by a suffix returns that table and suffix.
Every successful table read consumes exactly the corresponding table encoding.
The table reader and erased skipper agree on the remaining suffix.
Each table encoding has length at least 351 times the number of states.
Malformed strings denote the fixed fallback code.
